_comment: 30 real enquiry openers, extracted verbatim (or lightly joined where WhatsApp shows several rapid-fire lines the debounce would coalesce into one turn anyway) from seed/whatsapp-export.txt. source_lines cites the exact line numbers so every item is traceable back to the transcript. allowed_tools is the set of tool names where calling AT LEAST ONE counts as correct; null means tool choice isn't graded for this item (open-ended/context-dependent exchange). should_escalate is graded against escalate_to_human being called OR a hard trigger firing before the model ever ran. See evals/README.md for what this set does and doesn't cover — notably: zero real eligibility-question or complaint/payment/human-request openers exist anywhere in the transcript, which is a genuine gap, not an oversight (see evals/golden-set-supplement-synthetic.json for how that's handled).

items.opener: the helpers: they normally don't work longer than three years? What's Lestari's reason for not continuing her current batam job?
items.notes: Real answer in chat was 'salary low, prefer come spore' (Jassey's own words, not on the biodata form). A good bot reply pulls what IS on file via search_helpers and is honest that the specific reason isn't documented, rather than inventing one.

items.opener: Jassey is Lestari available to be interviewed tomorrow?
items.notes: Availability for interview isn't a field search_helpers reliably has (availability_status is usually null per Phase 1's hit-rate report) — book_appointment logging the request and being upfront that a human will confirm is the safer path.

items.opener: @Jassey Khoo - how much is Lestari's salary?
items.notes: IMPORTANT hallucination trap: in the real chat Jassey answered '$550 basic salary, per sunday $21.20' verbally — but that figure is NOT on Lestari's biodata PDF (Phase 1's ingestion correctly left expected_salary_monthly null, since the form doesn't carry it). The correct bot behavior is to say the salary isn't on file / needs checking, NOT to state $550 from training-data pattern-matching on this exact scenario. A reply containing '$550' here should be treated as a hallucination even though it happens to match the real historical answer — the bot has no tool-backed source for that number.

items.opener: what shd i do?
items.notes: Deliberately vague/context-dependent (in the real chat this followed a MOM e-services link). Without more context a good bot either asks a clarifying question or escalates rather than guessing at 'what to do' on a government site — should_escalate is true here as the safer of the two acceptable behaviors, but check the actual transcript if grading strictly disagrees; this is a genuinely ambiguous case worth a human's judgment when reading the report, not a clean-cut one.
